title.narrative: Supporting Independent Media and Information Resilience (SIMIR) in Moldova

description.narrative: Contract related to: Supporting Independent Media and Information Resilience (SIMIR) in Moldova - This 18-month measure aims to strengthen the Republic of Moldova¿s resilience to the crisis situation. It will support national efforts to increase the country¿s cyber- and information security while also providing inclusive assistance to the government and population in managing the refugee influx resulting from the war in Ukraine. In a first component, the measure will assist the establishment of a robust cyber threats monitoring and reaction mechanism (Cyber Security Operation Centre and/or national Computer Emergency Response Team ) under the responsibility of the Deputy Prime Minister for Digitalisation, to help identify possible cyberattacks and enable relevant authorities to launch and coordinate responsive action when necessary. In a second component, the action will support increased cooperation between government authorities, civil society, and the independent media, to increase media-literacy and to respond to disinformation. A third component will provide assistance to government authorities to ensure the inclusive hosting of recent arrivals from Ukraine, with a specific focus on strengthening the resilience of host-communities to mitigate deterioration in access to basic services linked to the refugee influx. This component will be implemented in close coordination with planned humanitarian and development cooperation assistance.

comment.narrative: The outcome was accomplished at a level of 5Fully surpassing the initial target. The undertaken activities in response to the emerging crisis triggered by Russias fullscale invasion of Ukraine demonstrated a wellcalibrated and effective approach. The decision to provide emergency assistance to professional independent media support community activities addressing disinformation and assist the AVC proved to be the appropriate response. The outcomes were in line with expectations as evidenced by two key achievements. Firstly independent media organisations sustained their uninterrupted production and dissemination of quality information ensuring that audiences had access to reliable news. Secondly the initiatives facilitated an improvement in residents ability to identify disinformation and resist malign influences thereby enhancing the overall resilience of the targeted communities. These results underscore the importance of strategic interventions in times of crisis to fortify media resilience and community resistance against the challenges posed by disinformation.

Internews conducted an informal internal gender analysis before awarding the subgrants for both emergency and disinformation funds. This approach ensured a nuanced understanding of potential gender implications and the diverse needs challenges and opportunities of the targeted audiences. Internews ensured that gender and diverse age ranges were represented by potential subgrantees while discussing the projects themselves. Thus the selected projects and organisations targeted youth adults and the elderly both women and men girls and boys in rural and urban communities. Internews considered the findings of this informal gender analysis in its further steps fostering a gendersensitive approach throughout the subgrant issuance process. For example during the execution of the Action subgrantees of the disinformation fund collected genderdisaggregated data. Thus Internews gained valuable insights into the compositions of SIMIR target communities allowing it to work with partners to tailor the interventions accordingly. Internews organised informal discussions with subgrantees who organised activities at the local level to take into consideration the communityspecific representation of boys and girls women and men.

title.narrative: A gender perspective was mainstreamed throughout the implementation of the intervention.

description.narrative: Obligatory for all crisis response and conflict prevention/peacebuilding/crisispreparedness actions

comment.narrative: Internews incorporated gender considerations across all its policies procedures and programming. Although the intervention did not include a standalone gender component subgrantees were mindful of the integration of gender considerations. As an example Moldova.org a subgrantee under the SIMIR emergency fund started with a website audience comprised of 65 females and 35 males. With SIMIR support their goal was to draw in more male users to achieve a balanced representation. By the end of September 2023 Moldova.org achieved a distribution of 42 men and 58 women by covering more mens health topics and other areas of mens interests. This ensured that opportunities and benefits were accessible to all genders men and women girls and boys equally fostering inclusivity. The approach aimed to be nondiscriminative promoting an environment where individuals were treated fairly and equitably regardless of gender. Through this the intervention attempted to contribute to a more inclusive and just society by addressing the diverse needs and experiences associated with various gender identities.

comment.narrative: The intervention shared information and coordinated with other multilateral institutions operating in Moldova such as People in Need PIN EED the Council of Europe in Moldova National Democratic Institute NDI the Independent Journalism Center IJC Deutsche Welle and the EUfunded project Strategic Communication and Support to MassMedia in the Republic of Moldova. Some representatives from these organisations even participated as members of the SIMIR grants selection committees ensuring a multistakeholder approach and diverse perspectives in decisionmaking processes. The project team also engaged with the US State Department the US Embassy the United States Agency for International Development USAID the Delegation of the European Union to the Republic of Moldova the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs and SIDA to coordinate support to local media. The multilateral multistakeholder approach not only strengthened collaboration among institutions but also enhanced the crucial need to empower residents with the skills necessary to navigate and critically assess information within the Moldovan media landscape. By combining efforts the intervention created a more resilient and informed community contributing to the broader goals of the project.

In response to this shift in emergency support Internews made the strategic decision to redistribute the budget among the remaining outlets. This decision was driven by the KPs challenges particularly the increased costs of bills during the winter and the higher prices resulting from inflation. By prioritising the needs of the current KPs Internews fortified their capacity to navigate financial challenges and continue contributing to the projects objectives.

The intervention employed a multilateral approach to improve resilience against propaganda and disinformation in Moldova. Internews used a multilateral approach while implementing the project by engaging with various stakeholders in Moldova to enhance resilience against propaganda and disinformation. On September 5 2022 Internews presented the Action at the media donors coordination meeting hosted by the International Media Support organisation a gathering of key stakeholders supporting media in Moldova. During the meeting Internews outlined its ongoing and upcoming activities within the SIMIR project utilizing tools like the matrix used by the donors to present supported media projects in Moldova. The matrix was updated in collaboration with the Delegation of the European Union to the Republic of Moldova and included details about the projects progress and plans with contributions from entities such as the Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency SIDA the UK Embassy the US Embassy the Soros Foundation the European Endowment for Democracy EED the Embassy of Finland the Swiss Cooperation Office in Moldova the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe OSCE the Embassy of Canada National Endowment for Democracy NED Deutsche Welle and Deutsche Gesellschaft fr Internationale Zusammenarbeit GmbH GIZ. During the project Internews continued collaboration with various stakeholders to leverage diverse perspectives and expertise to create a more effective strategy to improve resilience against propaganda.
